title: Accounts Administrator
description:
Blackburn Permanent Office-based

Are you an experienced Accounts Administrator looking for your next opportunity within a successful and growing business?

We are working with an established Lancashire-based business that has built a strong reputation within its specialist industry. With a busy operation and continued growth, they are now looking to appoint an Accounts Administrator to join their team and play an important role in supporting the day-to-day finance function.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys a varied accounts role, is highly organised and takes pride in getting things right.

The Role

Working as part of the finance team, you will provide day-to-day administrative and transactional support across the accounts function.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing invoices and financial transactions accurately and efficiently
- Supporting purchase and sales ledger activities (roughly 1800 per month)
- Matching invoices to purchase orders and delivery documentation
- Maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring information is kept up to date
- Assisting with account reconciliations
- Liaising with suppliers and customers regarding account queries
- Processing payments and supporting the wider finance team with finance administration
- Providing general administrative support to the finance function
- Working closely with colleagues across the wider business to resolve queries and ensure information is accurate

About You

We are looking for someone with previous experience within an accounts or finance administration position who is confident working with numbers and managing financial information accurately.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in an accounts administration or finance support role
- Good understanding of accounting processes
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time-management skills
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal
- A confident and professional approach when dealing with customers, suppliers and colleagues
- Good IT skills and experience using Microsoft Office, Knowledge of Sage 200 is beneficial

Most importantly, you will be someone who is reliable, proactive and keen to develop your career within a busy and established business.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £30,000
- 25 days annual leave + bank holidays
- Company pension
- Permanent, full-time position
- Office-based working environment
- Opportunity to join an established and growing Lancashire business
- Supportive team environment
- Excellent opportunity to develop your finance and accounts experience

If you are looking for a varied Accounts Administrator position where you can become a valued member of an established team, we would love to hear from you.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Temporary Position Part Time 1 Month 3 Days Per Week

Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant or Bookkeeper looking for a short-term, part-time temporary opportunity?

We're recruiting on behalf of a well-established and growing business for an Accounts & Payroll Administrator to join their friendly finance team on a temporary basis for around one month, working 3 days per week.

This is a varied, hands-on role where no two days are the same. If you enjoy rolling your sleeves up, working across multiple areas of finance and being part of a supportive team, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

As the Accounts & Payroll Administrator, you'll play an important role supporting the finance team with a broad range of accounting and payroll duties, helping to keep everything running smoothly throughout the assignment.

Your day-to-day will include:
- Processing purchase ledger invoices and supplier payments.
- Posting sales ledger receipts and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Handling supplier queries and resolving invoice discrepancies.
- Assisting with payroll administration and payroll processing.
- Processing employee expenses and posting transactions to the ledger.
- Maintaining cash books and financial records.
- Producing and updating sales, stock and purchase reports.
- Maintaining weekly and monthly Excel spreadsheets and management reports.
- Providing general administrative support to the wider finance team.
- Supporting colleagues across the business as required.

About You

You'll be organised, proactive and comfortable working independently within a busy finance environment.

We're looking for someone with:
- Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Bookkeeping or Finance Administration role.
- A good understanding of purchase ledger and sales ledger processes.
- Experience supporting payroll or payroll administration is highly desirable.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills and confidence working with spreadsheets.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to prioritise workloads and manage multiple tasks.
- A positive, flexible attitude and a willingness to help wherever needed.
- Experience using Sage 200 would be advantageous but isn't essential.

What's on Offer?
- 1 month temporary assignment.
- Part-time hours, 3 days per week.
- Flexible working days to be discussed.
- A varied role within a supportive finance team.
- The opportunity to gain further experience within a successful and growing business.
- Immediate start available.

Interested?

If you're immediately available and looking for a short-term, part-time assignment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact the Accountancy & Finance team at Cummins Mellor Recruitment for a confidential conversation about the opportunity.

title: Credit Control
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company
You'll be joining a long-established manufacturing and engineering business based in Blackburn, recognised for delivering high-quality products and services to customers across a range of industries throughout the UK and internationally. With a busy finance function and a sizeable customer base, the business is looking to appoint an experienced Credit Controller to support cash collection and customer account management on a temporary assignment for up to 6 months.

Your new role
Reporting to the Finance Manager, you will take responsibility for a high-volume ledger, ensuring outstanding debt is collected efficiently whilst maintaining excellent relationships with customers.
Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining a large sales ledger
- Proactively chasing outstanding debt via telephone and email
- Investigating and resolving customer queries and invoice disputes
- Allocating customer payments and reconciling accounts
- Producing aged debt reports and escalation reports for management
- Negotiating payment plans where appropriate
- Building strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders
- Supporting month-end reporting and cash flow management
- Reducing debtor days and improving overall collection performance
- Working closely with sales, operations and finance teams to resolve account issues

What you'll need to succeed
- Previous experience in a Credit Control position
- Strong communication
- Experience managing high-value and high-volume customer accounts
- Ability to build rapport with customers whilst maintaining a firm approach
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and finance systems
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills
- Available to start at short notice

What you'll get in return
- Salary equivalent of £30,000
- Immediate start available
- 6-month temporary contract
- Free on-site parking
- Full-time office-based role
- Opportunity to gain experience within a successful and growing manufacturing business
- Supportive and collaborative finance team

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller
Location: Blackburn
Salary: Up to £29,000 per annum
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Working Pattern: Hybrid - 3 days in the office / 2 days working from home after probation

Client Details

We are currently recruiting for an experienced and motivated Credit Controller to join a growing finance team in Blackburn.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with strong communication and organisational skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and is confident managing customer accounts, chasing outstanding payments and maintaining strong relationships with clients.

Description

The key responsibilities of a Credit Controller will include:
- Full ownership of a high-volume portfolio of customer accounts, managing the end-to-end credit control and collections process to maximise cash flow.
- Proactively pursue outstanding and overdue payments via telephone and email, resolving complex queries efficiently to reduce aged debt and consistently achieve collection targets, including negotiating payment plans in line with company policy.
- Work collaboratively with Sales, Operations and Customer Service teams to resolve account queries, remove payment barriers and facilitate timely customer payments.
- Accurately process and allocate incoming payments, ensuring customer accounts and ledgers are maintained to reflect an accurate and up-to-date financial position.
- Maintain comprehensive and accurate records of all credit control activity, customer communications, account statuses and collection actions.
- Produce and review regular aged debtor reports, monitoring portfolio performance and identifying overdue, high-value and potentially high-risk accounts requiring further action.
- Attend debtor meetings and manage escalated accounts, working proactively to resolve disputes and secure payment while maintaining strong and professional customer relationships.
- Provide support to the Credit Control Team Leader and Credit Control Manager on escalated accounts, ad-hoc tasks and wider credit control projects as required.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller will have:
- Proven credit control experience within a high-volume, high-value ledger environment.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workload and maximise cash collection.
- Excellent communication, problem-solving and dispute-resolution skills.
- Good Microsoft Excel skills with strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proactive, target-driven and results-focused approach.
- Flexible, enthusiastic and positive can-do attitude.
- Experience with SAP B1 is desirable.

Job Offer
- A salary range between £28,000 - £29,000 per annum
- Full time, permanent role
- Hybrid working - 3 days in office / 2 days working from home after probation pass
- Flexible core working hours
- Free on-site parking
- Growing and exciting business - opportunities to grow and progress

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
A good Purchase Ledger professional does a lot more than process invoices.

You're the person making sure suppliers get paid correctly, queries don't sit unanswered and the numbers going into the finance system are accurate. When something doesn't add up, you're usually the one who spots it and gets it sorted.

If you're organised, good with detail and like being part of a finance team where people actually work together, this could be a great next move.

You'll be joining an established team with experienced colleagues around you and supportive management. There's plenty to keep you busy, but you won't be expected to figure everything out on your own.

What will you be doing?

A big part of the role will be managing a high volume of supplier invoices, making sure they're processed accurately and within the right timescales.

You'll also be:
- Matching, checking and coding supplier invoices
- Responding to supplier queries over the phone and by email
- Keeping supplier records and account information accurate and up to date
- Investigating discrepancies and getting them resolved
- Working closely with finance and operational teams across the business
- Supporting the wider finance team with general administration when required
- Helping to keep payment processes running smoothly and on schedule

It's a busy role, so being able to stay organised and keep on top of your workload will be important. If you're someone who likes getting things ticked off, solving problems and knowing everything is where it should be, you'll probably enjoy it.

What are they looking for?

You'll already have some experience working within finance or accounts, ideally in a Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable position.

You'll also need:
- Previous Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable experience
- A good understanding of basic accounting processes
- Strong attention to detail and a focus on getting things right
- The ability to manage a busy workload and prioritise effectively
- Confidence working to deadlines

More than anything, they're looking for someone dependable who takes ownership of their work and can become a reliable part of the team.

What's in it for you?
- Salary of up to £28k, depending on experience
- 28 days' annual leave
- Hybrid working once you've completed your probation
- Opportunities to progress and develop your career

If this sounds like the sort of Purchase Ledger role you've been looking for, click "apply now" to find out more.
